title: Derived internal Hom on a ringed site
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site, $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$
its abelian category of sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules and $D(\mathcal O)$ the
derived category of $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$. For complexes
$\mathcal L^\bullet,\mathcal M^\bullet$ of $\mathcal O$-modules the *Hom complex*
$\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\mathcal L^\bullet,\mathcal M^\bullet)$ is the complex of
$\mathcal O$-modules with terms

$$
 \mathcal Hom^n(\mathcal L^\bullet,\mathcal M^\bullet)
 =\prod_{p\in\mathbf Z}\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal L^p,\mathcal M^{p+n})
$$

(sheaf Hom of $\mathcal O$-modules) and differential
$d(\varphi)=d_{\mathcal M}\circ\varphi-(-1)^n\varphi\circ d_{\mathcal L}$. A
complex $\mathcal I^\bullet$ of $\mathcal O$-modules is *K-injective* if every
map of complexes from an acyclic complex to $\mathcal I^\bullet$ is homotopic
to zero; every complex $\mathcal M^\bullet$ admits a quasi-isomorphism
$\mathcal M^\bullet\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ to a K-injective complex (a
*K-injective resolution*). For $L,M\in D(\mathcal O)$, represented by
$\mathcal L^\bullet$ and by a K-injective resolution $\mathcal I^\bullet$ of a
representative of $M$, the *derived internal Hom* is

$$
 R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(L,M)
 =\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\mathcal L^\bullet,\mathcal I^\bullet)\in D(\mathcal O);
$$

up to unique isomorphism it does not depend on the choices, and it is a functor
$D(\mathcal O)^{\mathrm{op}}\times D(\mathcal O)\to D(\mathcal O)$, with
$H^0(\mathcal C,R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(L,M))=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O)}(L,M)$.
